memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "But if she cannot afford a lamb, she is to bring two doves or two young pigeons, one for a burnt offering and the other for a sin offering. In this way the priest will make atonement for her, and she will be clean." - Lev 12:8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This last verse may be the most tender in the chapter. If she cannot afford a lamb. God anticipates the poor mother — and He does not lower her standing, only her cost. Two birds instead of a lamb, and the result is exactly the same: atonement made, and she will be clean.

No second-class cleansing. No lesser forgiveness for those with less money. In God's economy the poor are never further from His presence than the wealthy.

Now hold this verse next to something that happened roughly fourteen centuries later. A young mother came to the temple in Jerusalem with her newborn son, obeying this very law. And Luke records what she brought: a pair of doves or two young pigeons (Luke 2:24).

Mary brought the offering of the poor.

Think about what that means. The Son of God was not born into wealth or privilege. His mother could not afford a lamb — because she was carrying the Lamb. The One being presented in the temple that day would one day be the final offering that this entire system was pointing towards.

If you have ever felt you have too little to bring to God, look at Bethlehem. He came to the poor, as one of the poor, for all of us.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have you ever felt you had too little to offer God?
2. What does it mean to you that Jesus was born into an ordinary, poor family?
3. How should God's care for the poor shape the way your church and family live?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that Your grace has never been priced beyond anyone's reach. Thank You that Jesus came among the poor and became the Lamb we could never afford. Amen.
